en: Then, having caused the mandala ground to be smeared with fragrant substances and the like, and strewn with heaps of flowers, one should there, as far as possible, prepare square mandalas in the compartments for the five presiding deities.

For the other deities, having prepared a circular [mandala] with the five nectars and fragrances, one facing west should cause the mandala-circle to be drawn—brought there by rays from the seed-syllable in one's own heart—and having seated it as appropriate upon moons or suns situated on lotuses, worshiped it preceded by water for the feet and so forth, and praised it, one should taste the nectar. Then, placing the right knee on the ground, one should place the syllable *HŪṂ* on the tongue—which is like a single-pointed vajra—while holding a censer in the right hand and ringing the vajra-bell with the left.
[Then recite] the verse: *Oṃ*.

Then, having smeared the site of the mandala with fragrant scents and the like, and having had flowers strewn out in rows, one should construct a square maṇḍala there for the five lords as they appear in their respective effigies (liṭsa), while for the other deities it should be circular; this should be done with fragrant substances together with the five nectars (pañcāmṛta).

Facing west, one should invite the maṇḍala wheel—which is to be drawn there by the light rays from the seed-syllable at one’s own heart—to reside upon a lotus situated on either a moon or a sun disk, as appropriate for each maṇḍala; then, having performed the offerings preceded by the foot-washing water and so forth, along with praises and the tasting of nectar (amṛta).

Placing her right knee on the ground and making her tongue a single-pointed vajra born from the syllable *hūṃ*, she places the *hūṃ* there; holding a skull-cup with her right hand and ringing a vajra-bell with her left, she says:
"O Blessed One, O Vidyārāja Amukasa-vajra, homage be to you!
O Protector, I desire to paint the mandala whose nature is compassion."
Out of compassion for the disciples, for your own worship,
for the increase of the merit of sentient beings, and for the arising of the thought of awakening.
Therefore, O Blessed One, you ought to grant your grace to me, your devotee;
may the Buddhas, who bestow the purpose of the wheel of activity for the world, attend to me.
Bodhisattvas established in the fruit, as well as other mantra-deities,
deities, world-protectors, and spirits who are governed by perfect enlightenment.
O you beings with the vajra-eye who delight in the teaching, I am such-and-such a great Vajrin; [I shall enter] the mandala of such-and-such an arising.
For the purification of the world, I shall write this according to my capacity and with due ritual offerings;
therefore, out of compassion, may you all, together with your disciples, grant your presence within the mandala.

Bhagavān, Great Vajra, Supreme One, to you, the King of Knowledge, I bow. O Protector, whose very nature is compassion, I wish to draw the maṇḍala. For the sake of showing affection for my disciples, for the sake of making offerings to you, for the sake of increasing the merit of sentient beings, and for the sake of generating the mind of awakening—therefore, O Bhagavān, I am full of devotion.

May those who are worthy of being granted the grace of your command—the Buddhas who perform the welfare of wandering beings, the Bodhisattvas established in the fruit, and all other deities of secret mantra; the gods and the guardians of the world; the spirits who abide in the teaching of awakening; those sentient beings who take great delight in the teaching; and whoever possesses the vajra-eye—[may they all grant their blessings].

Please turn your perfect attention toward me! I am such-and-such a Vajra. For the sake of purifying wandering beings, I shall draw the maṇḍala from which the rituals arise, employing it according to my ability.
Thus, one should make the request by reciting this three times while bringing the meaning to mind.
Thus concludes the ritual procedure for the consecration of the deities.
Thus concludes the ritual for the further consecration (*adhivāsana*) of the deities.
